stem:
A 12-day-old newborn presents with a temperature of 38.3°C. He is slightly irritable but has no localizing signs.

What is the most appropriate management?

options.label: A
options.text: Full sepsis evaluation and start empiric IV antibiotics
options.explanation: Correct. Any febrile neonate needs urgent sepsis workup, admission, and empiric IV antibiotics because the risk of serious bacterial infection is high.

options.label: B
options.text: Discharge with oral antibiotics and outpatient follow-up
options.explanation: Outpatient oral treatment is unsafe in a 12-day-old with fever because occult serious infection must be assumed until excluded.

options.label: C
options.text: No evaluation is required if feeding is normal
options.explanation: Normal feeding does not rule out neonatal sepsis. Fever alone in this age group warrants investigation.

options.label: D
options.text: Give antipyretics only and observe at home
options.explanation: Symptomatic treatment alone would miss potentially life-threatening infection in a neonate.

options.label: E
options.text: Wait 48 hours to see if fever persists
options.explanation: Delaying investigation in a febrile neonate is unsafe because clinical deterioration can be rapid.

context: Febrile infants aged 28 days or younger by corrected age have a high risk of serious bacterial infection and require urgent blood, uncontaminated urine and CSF evaluation when safe, plus admission for empiric IV antibiotics.
